Idea.Title: Narrative is the recurrent visible locus of pipeline hierarchy drift
Idea.Description: Across the recorded runs, the Narrative stage most often contains the first observable departure from the requested company-first editorial hierarchy — turning a company introduction into an orchestration/product-led story, adding unsupported audiences or validation language, or strengthening factual claims introduced upstream.
Idea.Audience: Content ops leads, prompt engineers, editorial QA teams, and people running the Nuëyon.Compose pipeline experiments
Idea.Rationale: If Narrative is frequently the first stage where company-first intent becomes a product‑first or overclaimed story, then interventions targeted at Narrative (or at the upstream inputs that feed it) are the highest-leverage way to preserve story hierarchy and reduce downstream amplification of errors.
Idea.Evidence: Cross-experiment summary: the report explicitly states Narrative is the most recurrent first visible hierarchy shift (listed as first in Experiment 007 runs 001–002, Experiment 008 A-002, and multiple Experiment 009 baseline and candidate runs). Examples: 007 candidate 001 and 002 show Synthesis keeping company/product order but Narrative converts the through-line to “orchestration-focused/first”; 009 baselines and candidates often localize the first editorial/factual break to Narrative. Caveats and uncertainty: some runs drift earlier (Idea or Synthesis) — e.g., 008 A-001 and 008 A-003 show Idea-origin selection drift, and 007 candidate 003 shifts at Synthesis — and Experiment 007 lacks Idea/Research extracts, limiting traceability for those traces.
